claims.claim_text: The UK Government's Sovereign AI Venture Fund and the British Business Bank have backed Fractile, a London and Bristol-based AI chip startup, as part of a funding round worth over £500 million.
claims.excerpt: has secured backing from the UK Government’s Sovereign AI Venture Fund and the British Business Bank as part of a round worth over £500 million.

claims.claim_text: The government says the funding round values Fractile at over £5 billion.
claims.excerpt: Today’s funding round values the company at over £5 billion.

claims.claim_text: The round is a Series C that also includes investors CapitalG, Lightspeed and Redpoint.
claims.excerpt: it is also being backed through this Series C round by investors including CapitalG, Lightspeed and Redpoint.

claims.claim_text: The government says Fractile is re-inventing AI hardware to be faster, more energy efficient and less costly, taking a full-stack approach spanning chips, software and machine learning research.
claims.excerpt: Fractile is re-inventing the hardware that AI runs on, so that it is faster, more energy efficient, and less costly.

claims.claim_text: The government and the Business Bank say the investment will reduce reliance on overseas technology and strengthen UK sovereign capabilities in critical technologies.
claims.excerpt: reducing dependence on fragile overseas supply chains and ensuring the UK has a greater stake in the hardware that will underpin its future economy

claims.claim_text: The release says the specific investment amounts of Sovereign AI and the British Business Bank in Fractile are not disclosed because they are commercially sensitive.
claims.excerpt: Like most venture capital funds we do not comment on specific investment figures as they are commercially sensitive

claims.claim_text: Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds said Fractile has plans to expand its presence in Bristol.
claims.excerpt: With plans to expand their presence in Bristol, Fractile are helping to put our plans for reindustrialisation into action

claims.claim_text: The Chancellor confirmed at the Budget a further £140 million for Sovereign AI, including £60 million to support the Fund's investments and £80 million for its R&D Procurement Scheme.
claims.excerpt: the Chancellor confirmed a further £140 million backing for Sovereign AI, with an additional £60 million to support the Fund’s investments, plus £80 million for Sovereign AI’s R&D Procurement Scheme.

claims.claim_text: The Budget also expanded the British Business Bank's investment capacity by £5 billion to £30.6 billion.
claims.excerpt: The Chancellor also expanded the British Business Bank’s investment capacity by £5 billion to £30.6 billion

claims.claim_text: The government says Sovereign AI will expand into a new focus area of Physical and Industrial AI.
claims.excerpt: The Chancellor also announced that Sovereign AI would expand into a new focus area of Physical and Industrial AI
